message.content: {"rules":["Implementors of TrustedRandomAccess must ensure that the iterator's size_hint is exact.","Implementors of TrustedRandomAccess must ensure that the iterator's size_hint is cheap to call.","Implementors of TrustedRandomAccess must not override TrustedRandomAccessNoCoerce::size.","All subtypes and all supertypes of Self must also implement TrustedRandomAccess. For types with non-invariant parameters, bounds used to condition the implementation must preserve this requirement; the documentation identifies bounds from the struct/enum definition and bounds on traits with a similar guarantee as exceptions to the usual inability to depend on parameter trait bounds.","If Self: ExactSizeIterator, self.len() must always produce results consistent with self.size().","If Self: Iterator, callers of <Self as Iterator>::__iterator_get_unchecked(&mut self, idx) must ensure 0 <= idx and idx < self.size().","If Self: Iterator and Self: !Clone, callers must not call self.__iterator_get_unchecked(idx) more than once with the same index. Calls on self and values resulting from coercing self to supertypes, including successive coercion results, count together toward this limit.","If Self: Iterator, after self.__iterator_get_unchecked(idx) is called, callers may call self.next_back() at most self.size() - idx - 1 times. If Self: Clone and self is cloned, the limit is calculated separately for self and its clone, but next_back() calls before cloning count for both. Calls on a value and its successive coercion results count together toward this limit.","If Self: Iterator, after self.__iterator_get_unchecked(idx) is called, the only methods callers may call on self or any new clones of self are Clone::clone, Iterator::size_hint, DoubleEndedIterator::next_back, ExactSizeIterator::len, Iterator::__iterator_get_unchecked, and TrustedRandomAccessNoCoerce::size. The same restriction applies to values obtained by subsequently coercing self to a supertype, including through multiple coercion steps.","If Self is a subtype of T, callers are permitted to coerce self to T, including after an __iterator_get_unchecked call. Multiple such coercion steps are permitted, subject to the post-access method restrictions and aggregated unchecked-access and next_back limits.","If Self: Iterator, implementors must make <Self as Iterator>::__iterator_get_unchecked(&mut self, idx) safe to call when the index bounds, non-Clone repeated-index restriction, next_back limits, post-access method restrictions, and coercion accounting requirements are satisfied.","If Self: Iterator, an __iterator_get_unchecked call satisfying the index bounds, non-Clone repeated-index restriction, next_back limits, post-access method restrictions, and coercion accounting requirements must not change the value returned by size_hint.","If Self: Iterator, after an __iterator_get_unchecked call satisfying the index bounds, non-Clone repeated-index restriction, next_back limits, post-access method restrictions, and coercion accounting requirements, it must remain safe to call Clone::clone, Iterator::size_hint, DoubleEndedIterator::next_back, ExactSizeIterator::len, Iterator::__iterator_get_unchecked, and TrustedRandomAccessNoCoerce::size on self, assuming the required traits are implemented and those access constraints continue to be met.","If Self: Iterator, it must be safe to drop self after an __iterator_get_unchecked call satisfying the index bounds, non-Clone repeated-index restriction, next_back limits, post-access method restrictions, and coercion accounting requirements.","If Self: Iterator and Self is a subtype of T, it must be safe to coerce self to T after an __iterator_get_unchecked call satisfying the index bounds, non-Clone repeated-index restriction, next_back limits, post-access method restrictions, and coercion accounting requirements."]}
